title: Hotels: reception & housekeeping
_note: English for work (english-for-work run, 2026-11-02): written by hand in British English, not yet checked by a second reader. translations.en = short definition in simple English; deHint = German translation (the 'German' tab). Words that already exist in the English lexicon are refs with a job-specific example.
intro: The words for work in a hotel: reception, rooms, check-in, cleaning and talking to guests and colleagues. Every word has an example sentence from a real working day in the UK.
introEasy: Do you work in a hotel? Learn the words for rooms, guests and cleaning here.
tipps: At reception, start with a smile and a short greeting: “Good morning, how can I help you?” Guests remember how you speak to them.
If you do not understand a guest, ask politely: “Sorry, could you say that again, please?” It is better to ask than to guess.
When you must say no, say what you CAN do: “I'm afraid the room isn't ready yet, but I can look after your bags.”
